title: Peter Seah to retire as DBS chairman after 16 years; Anthony Lim to succeed him
text:

 Subscribe Peter Seah to retire as DBS chairman after 16 years; Anthony Lim to succeed him
 Currently a board member, Lim will assume the chairmanship on Jan 1, 2027

 Peter Seah (left) will be appointed senior adviser for a year. Anthony Lim has served on the DBS board since April 2020. IMAGE: DBS 
 [SINGAPORE] Peter Seah will retire as chairman of DBS’ board after 16 years in the role, the bank said in a filing on Thursday (Nov 5), the same day it released its third-quarter results .
 He will be succeeded by Anthony Lim, a current board member , on Jan 1, 2027.
 Seah, 80, will retire on Dec 31, 2026, and will be appointed senior adviser for a year.
 He noted that one of the board’s most important responsibilities is ensuring continuity of leadership.
 “Having completed the CEO transition to Su Shan, the bank is now entering its next chapter from a position of strength,” he said.
 “I am therefore able to hand over the reins to Anthony with confidence, knowing that DBS is in very capable hands.”

 As chairman since 2010, Seah provided “steadfast leadership and strategic oversight” as DBS pursued a strategy of digital transformation and growth in high-return businesses, the bank said.
 He is also currently the chairman of Singapore Airlines and Lasalle College of the Arts.
 Lim has served on the DBS board since April 2020, and sits on the board executive committee, board risk management committee and compensation and management development committee (CMDC).

 More As chairman of the CMDC, he has played a key role in management succession planning, including the CEO transition, as well as remuneration governance and talent development, DBS said.
 Prior to his retirement from executive roles in 2017, he held senior leadership roles at GIC and Bankers Trust, with assignments in Singapore, London and New York.
 DBS CEO Tan Su Shan said Lim has “consistently brought invaluable perspectives” on a wide range of issues, from geopolitics and risk management to organisational leadership and talent development in board deliberations over the years.
 In a letter of appreciation, Temasek CEO Dilhan Pillay and chairman Teo Chee Hean said Seah’s contributions to DBS were “both profound and enduring”.
 Apart from its strong financial performance, the bank pursued a clear strategic vision with the discipline to see it through under his tenure, they said.
 “Good chairmanship is often not immediately visible and oftentimes underappreciated,” they added. “It is reflected in the quality of decisions made, the difficult moments navigated, the leaders developed and the culture sustained.”
 Meanwhile, former DBS CEO Piyush Gupta said he “couldn’t have asked for a better partner and mentor”.
 He added: “He was the force behind our culture change, giving us the confidence to be bold and to invest for the future.”
